description.narrative: Organisationen för amerikanska staters särskilda fredsmission i Colombia (MAPP/OAS) har inkommit med en förfrågan till den svenska ambassaden i Bogotá om finansiering om 30 miljoner SEK för att stödja genomförandet av deras strategiska plan 2016–2021. Finansieringen gäller under perioden 1 juli 2019 – 21 december 2021. Syftet med insatsen är att bidra till genförandet av Colombias fredspolitik genom uppföljning, medföljning och stöd till specifika insatser inom utvalda tematiska områden. Genom att lämna rekommendationer till colombianska staten vill MAPP/OAS stärka förutsättningarna för en långvarig och hållbar fred, i enlighet med mandatet mellan Organisationen för amerikanska stater och Colombias regering. Verksamheten fokuserar på följande tre huvudområden: fredsbyggande; säkerhetsförhållanden och territoriell dynamik; övergångsrättvisa samt avväpning, demobilisering och återintegrering (DDR).

The intervention supports the implementation of MAPP/OAS´s country programme (Organization of American States/Mission to Support the Peace Process in Colombia) . Its primary objective is to assist the Colombian government in its implementation of the peace policy through comprehensive monitoring, accompaniment, and support for targeted activities across key thematic areas. The OAS-mission provides strategic recommendations to the Government of Colombia for the consolidation of a lasting peace. The country programme focuses on three main areas: Peacebuilding; Security conditions and territorial dynamics; and transitional justice, including disarmament, demobilization, and reintegration (DDR). A gender perspective is integrated throughout the country programme, both in staff recruitment and in the design and implementation of activities.

The main objective of the Mission to support the Peace Process of the Organization of American States (MAPP/OAS) is to support the Colombian States peace policy to contribute to the consolidation of a long-lasting peace. This will be achieved through specific results planned in the three main thematic areas: 1) Peacebuilding 2) Security conditions and territorial dynamics 3)Transitional Justice and disarmament, demobilization and reintegration (DDR) The activities within these areas are implemented through a comprehensive monitoring, accompaniment, and support, by the 18 regional offices in the country and the central office in Bogotá.

sector.narrative: Civilian peace-building, conflict prevention and resolution

description.narrative:
The achieved results are assessed as satisfactory in relation to the objectives of the intervention and its overall purpose. The contribution supported MAPP/OAS in fulfilling its core objective of accompanying the Colombian States peace policy, in line with the Missions mandate and overall intervention logic. This assessment is consistent with findings from previous evaluations of the Missions work, which highlight MAPP/OAS relevance, value added and effectiveness in complex and conflictaffected contexts (UM2019/17800/BOGO/109).
The results achieved reflect MAPP/OAS continued role as a trusted and relevant peace support mechanism, particularly through its territorial presence, monitoring and dialogue functions. These elements constitute core sources of the Missions added value and reinforce its contribution to peacerelated processes at both national and territorial levels.
The contribution reached diverse population groups, including victims of the armed conflict, women, ethnic communities and rural populations, primarily by supporting dialogue, participation and engagement with state institutions and peacerelated mechanisms. As confirmed by the evaluation, this has contributed to improved coordination among institutional actors and more informed decision making in peacebuilding processes.
The use of funds is assessed as reasonable and relevant in relation to the results achieved. According to the approved final financial reporting and audit, Sweden had a remaining balance of USD 322 as of 31 December 2024 (UM2019/17800/BOGO/181). In line with the Basket Fund statutes and the provisions of the agreementwhere Sida approves that financial management is carried out in accordance with the procedures established by the OAS General Secretariat, as reflected in Amendment No. 3, Article 6 on Financial Reporting (UM2019/17800/BOGO/115)balances below USD 1,000 are not subject to repayment. The final financial report has therefore been approved accordingly (UM2019/17800/BOGO/ 180).
Regarding the component related to the National Conciliation Committee (CCN), the support was agreed as part of the approved Plan and Budget (UM2019/17800/BOGO/163) and subsequent decisions by the Basket Fund members. A specific component was created in PlanIT for this purpose (12528A0104).
In the final financial reporting, the costs related to CCN are reflected as programme expenditures under Special Support to Dialogue and Negotiation Processes, in line with a dialogue among Basket Fund members held on 30 April 2024 and an amendment to the Basket Fund statutes (UM2019/17800/ BOGO/170).
As agreed between Sida and MAPP/OAS in a meeting held on 29 January 2024, there was no separate audit report for the CCN project. Instead, the related expenditures were included in the sample of the Basket Fund audit (UM2019/17800/BOGO/163). The external audit confirms the overall financial position of the contribution, including a final balance of USD 322, with no audit observations related to this component.
The support to CCN concluded in 2024 and was not continued under the subsequent phase of cooperation.
The achieved results, together with the continued strategic relevance of the Mission, informed Sidas decision to enter into a new agreement with MAPP/ OAS, signed on 8 May 2025, with an activity period from 1 January 2025 to 31 December 2026 (UM2024/29595/BOGO13). This reflects an overall assessment that the contribution delivered results aligned with its objectives and provided sufficient value to justify continued engagement. Regarding sustainability, many of the results achieved are institutional and relational in nature, including strengthened dialogue mechanisms, coordination practices and analytical capacities. As highlighted in the evaluation, such results are more likely to be sustained over time as they are embedded in institutional practices and relationships rather than being dependent on individual activities (UM2019/17800/BOGO/106 & UM2019/17800/BOGO/109)
